title: Lawn parties
summary: Williams describes lawn parties in the yard, with girls in gingham, knickerbockers and ribbons, and prizes for the best waltzers.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah, I read an article by a man called, his name was Jean Paul Sartre, and he wrote that up. I forgot what paper it is, I have it written down. It's cool. Anyway, he wrote that thing up, you know? Yeah. And they were making the film there. Yeah. And, uh, oh let's see, there's so many guys I want to ask you about. What was the Lawn Party like back in those days?

Oh, Lawn Party said, well, uh, gonna have a bone dance. Uh, the girls buy a gingham. Uh, you got shirts, you see, like it is now, uh, blue gingham. Uh, and some black and white. Uh, and they wore knickerbockers.

And they wore the dresses short, with a big boy in the back of their, back of their dress. Uh, uh, big boy ribbing in their head, socks, baby dog shoes. Uh, and, uh, they used to have prizes given for the best waltzers and the best shortists. And, uh, everybody would be dressed sometimes, four or five girls, and they'd all get their dresses made to light. Uh, some different clubs would be invited, and they'd come and they'd all be dressed up in the head, big boys of ribbons in their head, you know. So they called it that, and the boys with old hoes on, and red hankches, some had blue hankches, and sun hats on the head, big sun hats. They called it the bone dance. And some of them used to have red patches on the knee, you know, take a piece of red goods, and they'd come out comical, just like Mardi Gras, you know.
And they called out a bone dance.
Would that be inside or outside?
That would be in the yard.
In the yard, that'd be a lawn party.
Ah, I got it straight, huh?
